history.summary: The Hathikhana Kailash Temple is a Shiva temple in Ambala Cantt (Sadar), on Cross Road 12 near the old BD flour mill. Per its recorded local history (single-source: visitor reviews on worldorgs.com - verify), it is linked to the movement of British troops from Karnal to Ambala: South Indians serving with the British Elephant Cavalry Regiment were stationed near the BD flour mill, and the elephants were looked after by South Indian mahouts who were devotees of Lord Shiva. A small Shiva pindi was first installed in a hut, then in a proper temple named Hathi Khana Shiv Mandir. After the regiment moved on, local priests cared for the temple until 1950, after which a registered trust took over. The temple is listed as 'Hathi Khana Shiv Mandir' among Haryana's heritage structures by INTACH. It is known for lavish Mahashivratri decoration and heavy crowds on Mondays. TOWN CORRECTION: CSV town 'Ambala' is generic; the temple is in the Ambala Cantt (Sadar) area, so town is recorded as Ambala Cantt.

town_description: Ambala Cantonment (Ambala Cantt), together with Ambala City, forms the twin-city of Ambala in Haryana, about 3 km apart. Established by the British in 1843, it is one of India's oldest and largest cantonments with a strong Army and Air Force presence, and is known as a major commercial hub for cloth and scientific instruments.
